items.title: Vince DiMartino interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 8, 2025
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] My name is Monk Rowe for the Fillius Jazz Archive and I’m very pleased to have Vince DiMartino with me today.

ctx.x: I’m going to let you tell me.

Well in most liberal arts colleges they usually don’t have one but I taught in Centres so I know that they don’t really have them. They have an academic counsel or something you know. But at State universities you know you have to treat everybody equally meaning from the standpoint of the coursework. You can’t say, “Oh, well Monk you know you’re not a very good reader so I’m going to give you this real easy thing to do and then at the end of the semester you can write a one-page summary of what we did this…

other young person comes in, maybe the class is philosophy. “Well your mom and dad were both philosophers and they wrote books and things, so you have to read War and Peace and you have to tell me all the levels that this book is written on.” And then the guy that does the War and Peace gets a B, and guy that does the easy assignments because they just had no contact with music gets an A. You see that’s not fair. Just because that person is able you cannot treat them differently. So I wanted to make sure — and…
